is the most commonly used average. When people say "average" in everyday life, they usually mean the mean. It takes into account every value in the dataset, making it a useful summary -- but also making it sensitive to extreme values.

For example, if five friends earn $\pounds 20\,000$, $\pounds 22\,000$, $\pounds 25\,000$, $\pounds 23\,000$, and $\pounds 210\,000$, the mean salary is $\pounds 60\,000$, which doesn't represent any of them well. This is why understanding the mean's strengths and limitations is important.

Class A has 20 students with a mean mark of 64. Class B has 30 students with a mean mark of 72. Find the overall mean mark for both classes combined.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Total for Class A} &= 20 \times 64 = 1280 \\
\text{Total for Class B} &= 30 \times 72 = 2160 \\
\text{Combined total} &= 1280 + 2160 = 3440 \\
\text{Combined number} &= 20 + 30 = 50
\end{aligned}$$
The overall mean is NOT $\frac{64 + 72}{2} = 68$. You cannot just average the two means because the groups have different sizes. This is a very common exam question.
